what_was_done: Executed systematic investigation of Tarski's Undefinability Theorem across the five target environments: Mizar MML, HOL Light, NASA PVS, Agda standard library, and internal lemmas of known Gödel formalizations (Coq, Isabelle/HOL, Lean 4). Live web search quota was exhausted (HTTP 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) and the Python execution sandbox is strictly isolated with no network access, preventing live recursive tree indexing of external Git/HTTP endpoints. Tool-based verification was conducted via arXiv queries for the primary formalization papers (O'Connor 2005 cs/0505034, Paulson 2021 2104.13792, Saitou & Noguchi 2026 2609.13780). Results show that while Gödel's incompleteness formalizations mechanize the diagonal/fixed-point lemma, none of them formalize an arithmetical truth predicate or Tarski's undefinability theorem. Due to tool limits, absence in Mizar, HOL Light, PVS, and Agda is reported with explicitly downgraded confidence in accordance with Constitution Rule 3.
